subsystems.name: Bundle layer
subsystems.role: stores and forwards whole messages, taking custody so data survives broken links.

subsystems.name: Contact scheduling and routing
subsystems.role: predicts when links exist and computes paths across the network.

subsystems.name: Convergence layer adapters
subsystems.role: maps bundles onto specific radio or optical links.

subsystems.name: Security
subsystems.role: protects bundles while they sit on relay nodes and cross links.

subsystems.name: Network management
subsystems.role: lets operators monitor, configure and diagnose nodes that cannot be reached in real time.

subsystems.name: Application interface
subsystems.role: lets mission software send and receive data without managing links itself.

buildSteps.title: Specify the protocol
buildSteps.detail: Standards define the bundle format, custody transfer, routing, security and convergence layers so different agencies' nodes can interoperate.

buildSteps.title: Implement bundle agents
buildSteps.detail: Software is written for each spacecraft, lander or relay to hold bundles in memory or flash and run routing logic.

buildSteps.title: Write convergence-layer drivers
buildSteps.detail: Each physical link needs a driver that frames bundles for that radio or optical terminal and handles link-specific retransmission.

buildSteps.title: Build contact-plan tools
buildSteps.detail: Orbital mechanics and link budgets are turned into schedules of when each pair of nodes can talk.

buildSteps.title: Integrate security
buildSteps.detail: Bundle Protocol Security is added so bundles can be authenticated and encrypted even after passing through untrusted relays.

buildSteps.title: Test in emulation
buildSteps.detail: A testbed simulates hours-long delays, intermittent contacts and node failures to verify store-and-forward behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Fly demonstrations
buildSteps.detail: The stack is run on the International Space Station and on relay satellites to prove it works across real links.

buildSteps.title: Operate and extend
buildSteps.detail: Deployed nodes are managed, contact plans updated, and the network grows as new relays are launched.

prerequisites.why: it defines how bundles are formatted, stored and forwarded across disconnected nodes.
they provide the physical transport over which bundles travel.
higher-rate laser links will let future DTN nodes move far more data per contact.
store-and-forward requires memory and computing on each node.
routing depends on knowing when links will exist; predictions must be accurate over long horizons.
bundle security must work without real-time key exchange or online certificate checks.

pathway.milestone: BPv7 standardized and DTN experiments flown on the International Space Station

pathway.unlocks: near-continuous communications for landers and rovers on the far side and poles.

pathway.milestone: deep-space relay orbiters running DTN end to end
pathway.unlocks: reliable Mars and outer-planet data return without a live path from Earth.

pathway.milestone: a solar-system internet of interoperable relays
pathway.unlocks: human exploration and many robotic missions sharing one communications fabric.
